new_results.statement: For any invertible p-coordinate physical principal pivot, the Schur complement retains at least N_abs(A;L)-p eigenvalues at the identical threshold L, and separately at least N_+(A;L)-p positive and N_-(A;L)-p negative threshold eigenvalues.

If a final physical 3x3 principal block has sigma_min>=sigma, arbitrary outside spectrum/couplings give ||p_Q||inf<=6sqrt(pi)/sigma. A baseline triple with local added footprint delta<kappa gives 6sqrt(pi)/(kappa-delta).
If a scalar pivot has magnitude |a| and its Schur complement has a protected physical 3x3 block with sigma_min>=sigma, then ||p_Q||inf<=4sqrt(6sqrt(pi)/(|a|sigma)).

partner_result_applied.equation: M(h)<=6sqrt(pi)/sigma implies ||p_(U+psi(Z))||inf<=6sqrt(pi)/sigma for the arbitrary dependent outside quadratic remainder.

unresolved_implication: Prove N3: a universal density bound in the no-tau-pivot three-large-eigenvalue hybrid/dense class. The new Schur theorem shows extra large eigenvalues can be peeled without threshold degradation, but does not construct product-preserving smoothing in N3.
next_mechanism: Combine threshold-preserving physical Schur peeling with grouped-bank or weighted-volume certificates inside N3, paying the account04/B12 mixed norm only after product aggregation.
